sentences.text: Arenysuchus is an extinct genus of crocodylomorph that lived during the late Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous in northern Spain.
The genus is known from a partial skull, which serves as the holotype—the specimen the species is based on—and four teeth found at the Blasi 2 site.
This animal shares a feature with early crocodilians where the frontal bones contact the margins of the supratemporal fenestrae.
The frontal bone of Arenysuchus is unusual because its front end is extremely long.
Near the frontal bone, the lacrimal bones of Arenysuchus are unusually wide compared to their length.
The infratemporal bar of Arenysuchus is very thin and vertically expanded, unlike the thicker, laterally expanded bars of most other crocodilians.
Arenysuchus can be distinguished by an infratemporal bar that is tabular, vertically oriented, and has extreme lateromedial compression.
A sharp projection of the frontal bone divides the nasal bones, which make up most of the midline snout length.
The fossil remains of Arenysuchus were discovered in the Tremp Formation at Arén, Huesca, Spain, by researchers José Manuel Gasca and Ainara Badiola.
Arenysuchus was first named and described by Eduardo Puértolas, José I. Canudo, and Penélope Cruzado-Caballero in 2011.
The generic name Arenysuchus refers to the place of its discovery combined with the Greek term 'suchus', which translates to crocodile.
The specific epithet of Arenysuchus honors the researchers who discovered the holotype.
Dinosaurs were abundant in the environment, including a diversity of sauropods, theropods, and ornithopods.
With the formation of the archipelago, a faunal change occurred in the Late Maastrichtian, where dinosaurs became rarer, represented mainly by hadrosaurs.
Crocodilians became a major component of the island ecosystems.
In its original 2011 analysis, Arenysuchus was classified as one of the most basal members of the superfamily Crocodyloidea.
Subsequent phylogenetic studies have debated the classification of Arenysuchus, finding it to be the sister taxon of Allodaposuchus and a member of Allodaposuchidae.
Arenysuchus is classified within the family Allodaposuchidae.
Along with Prodiplocynodon, it is known from the Late Cretaceous, making them the oldest known crocodyloids.
Its parent group is Allodaposuchidae.
It belongs to the family Allodaposuchidae.
During the late Maastrichtian, Europe existed as an island archipelago surrounded by shallow seas.
The Tremp Formation, where Arenysuchus fossils were found, dates to the late Cretaceous and has been dated using planktonic foraminifers and magnetostratigraphy.
The Elias site, where the holotype was found, dates from approximately 67.6 to 65.5 million years ago.
It lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
By the end of the Maastrichtian, Europe consisted of a series of island archipelagos surrounded by shallow seas.
